title: Minimax Inference for Latent-Mediator Effects in Panels under Label Ambiguity
banked_reason: D-0.5 angle 0 exhausted five revisions with REVISE; inherited assignment-fiber and point-ID extrema remained duplicated solve targets despite repeated demotion directives.
gap_reasons: The sharp residual-label assignment fiber with positive-completion attainment duplicates the kernel of eid_hiddenoutcome_labelsync_complete; its mediation cost is a specialization.
The tied-block alternating-contrast criterion and assignment extrema duplicate eid_hiddenoutcome_labelsync_complete's additive assignment-cost criterion and sharp orbit image.
proof_attempt_summary: Five D-0.5 revisions developed a common-weight branch map, a local inference program, and an explicit joint Gaussian confidence report. The reviewer kept the proposal at REVISE because two already-known assignment results remained to-prove solve targets after repeated directives to demote them. The revision cap ended this run before D0 or Lean formalization; a future independent run can cite those prerequisites outside its solve targets and test the remaining inference claims.
tldr: Armwise three-block recovery identifies independent treatment-specific permutation orbits. Conditional on maintained latent-stratum mediator exchangeability, those orbits yield an exact weight-preserving causal assignment fiber, positive causal completions, an alternating-contrast point-identification criterion, and assignment extrema; these are credited preliminary specializations of \(\texttt{eid\_hiddenoutcome\_labelsync\_complete}\), not headline results. The contribution is the inference frontier on the explicitly common-weight branch image \(\Gamma_s\): a common projected-influence-function iff for regular estimation, a compact-uniform nuisance-adjusted finite-table Le Cam reduction, its target-scaled minimax risk, and an exact branch report calibrated from the transported joint four-dimensional gap--target influence vector. The single uniform max event gives scalar coverage off a tie, simultaneous two-branch coverage at a tie, and a matching first-order diameter lower bound. Without the empirically untestable mediator-exchangeability judgment, the mixture recovery and branch-inference results remain statistical but the causal interpretation of \(\psi\) does not follow. The multiclass permutation experiment remains the explicit open frontier.
gap: Published tensor methods recover each arm only up to an independently chosen permutation, while the internal label-synchronization result already supplies the assignment-set foundation. Existing ATE sensitivity analysis for discrete unobserved confounding is adjacent rather than a matching theorem for this panel. What remains absent is a target-sensitive inference theory when otherwise regular armwise mixtures meet at a common weight tie: neither smooth mediation efficiency theory nor generic weak-identification theory supplies the common projected derivative, the profiled finite-table experiment, or honest coverage with a matching diameter obstruction.
fill: The contribution is the common-EIF regularity boundary, the compact-uniform nuisance-adjusted two-sign Le Cam experiment on the valid common-weight map \(\Gamma_s\), its attained target-valued minimax risk, and branch inversion calibrated by the joint four-dimensional Gaussian maximum with matching first-order diameter lower bounds.
